subject.title: fix(auth): cooldown inline api key billing failures

question: Should inline API keys inherit the existing persistent billing cooldown unchanged, or must this PR include a supported recovery path after a user restores provider credit?
rationale: The branch deliberately fail-closes an inline key for the configured cooldown, while the author identifies no success-clear or manual-clear counterpart; choosing whether that parity is acceptable is product and recovery-policy judgment rather than a mechanical patch decision.

options.title: Land cooldown parity; track recovery separately
options.body: Accept the existing profile-cooldown semantics for inline keys after final-head proof, and resolve recovery design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/70903.

options.title: Require recovery before merge
options.body: Add and prove a supported reset, half-open probe, or other recovery mechanism before extending persistent cooldowns to inline-only configurations.

options.title: Narrow the PR to marking only
options.body: Defer fail-closed enforcement until maintainers choose the recovery contract, at the cost of leaving the original retry-loop protection incomplete.

recommendation.title: Land cooldown parity; track recovery separately
recommendation.body: Accept the existing profile-cooldown semantics for inline keys after final-head proof, and resolve recovery design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/70903.

likelyOwner.reason: The author has documented the concrete recovery trade-offs and can implement the chosen bounded direction, though approval should come from a maintainer responsible for auth behavior.
